issues.description: The problem statement and reference solution use the name create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate for the two-qubit gate tensor factory, but the template implementation defines the function as create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate. This mismatch of identifiers for the same conceptual entity (a nearest-neighbor / adjacent two-qubit gate tensor) creates an unnecessary mapping burden: students reading the problem and tests will look for create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate, while the template exposes a differently named implementation. This can cause confusion and lead students to (a) search for a non-existent symbol, (b) duplicate work by implementing the expected name in addition to the provided one, or (c) fail automated tests that expect the canonical name.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Rename the template function from create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate to create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate (and update any internal references and the docstring). Alternatively, if you prefer the 'adjacent' wording, update the problem statement and solution to use create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate everywhere. Preferably align the template to the problem/tests by renaming the function to create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate.
